subject: Emotions
title: The Contamination Instinct
description: A quick win: understand The Contamination Instinct.

hook.text: Would you wear a sweater once worn by a serial killer—even after it's been washed ten times?

buildup.text: Most people say no. The 'essence' of the killer seems to linger despite all physical cleaning.

discovery.text: Psychologists call this the 'law of contagion.' Once two things touch, they share properties forever.

twist.text: It works positively too. People pay more for a sweater if told a celebrity once wore it.

climax.text: Contamination thinking is ancient. It predates germ theory by thousands of years.

punchline.text: We invented hygiene from a feeling, not from science.

quiz.question: What psychological principle explains contamination thinking?
